title: Hokkien Mee (Hokkien Noodles)
description: Hokkien Mee is a popular Southeast Asian noodle dish featuring thick yellow noodles stir-fried with succulent pork, shrimp, vegetables, and a rich savory sauce. Cooked with high heat for authentic wok hei, this dish delivers smoky aromas, deep umami flavor, and perfectly coated noodles in every bite.

ingredients.title: For the Protein
items: Pork shoulder or pork belly – 150 g, thinly sliced

ingredients.title: For the Noodles
items: Fresh Hokkien yellow noodles – 300 g, rinsed and drained (or thick egg noodles as a substitute)

ingredients.title: For Vegetables & Aromatics
items: Chinese kale or baby bok choy – 100 g, cut into 2-inch pieces

ingredients.title: For Garnish
items: Fresh chili in vinegar or prik nam som (Thai chili vinegar)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Sauce
steps: Combine light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, fish sauce, stock, and white pepper in a small bowl.
Mix well and set aside for later use.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Cooking the Protein
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add pork slices and stir-fry until almost cooked.
Add shrimp and squid if using, then cook until seafood is just turning pink.
Remove the protein from the wok and set aside.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Stir-Frying Aromatics & Vegetables
steps: Add a little more oil to the same wok.
Sauté garlic and onion until fragrant and lightly softened.
Add Chinese kale and stir-fry briefly for about 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and toss well with the vegetables.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Combining the Dish
steps: Return the cooked protein to the wok.
Pour the prepared sauce over the noodles.
Toss everything together over high heat until the noodles absorb the sauce and develop a slightly smoky wok flavor.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the sauce reduces and coats the noodles evenly.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Final Seasoning
steps: Taste and adjust seasoning with extra sugar or fish sauce if needed.
Drizzle with sesame oil for extra aroma if desired.
Add bean sprouts just before serving to maintain their fresh crunch.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Serving
steps: Transfer the noodles to serving plates.
Top with fried shallots.
Serve hot with lime wedges and chili vinegar on the side.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately from the wok while the noodles are still smoky and glossy.
Pair with lime wedges and chili vinegar to balance the rich savory flavors.
Add extra fried shallots and fresh herbs for a restaurant-style presentation.

chefTips: High heat is essential for authentic wok hei — use a large wok and avoid overcrowding.
Do not overcook shrimp; they should remain juicy, firm, and just pink.
Slightly charred noodles add depth and the signature smoky flavor of great Hokkien Mee.
Fresh stock creates a richer sauce compared with plain water.
Rinse fresh noodles briefly before cooking to prevent clumping while maintaining their chewy texture.
